title: 3.4.5 Lab: Rewrite a Declaration as an Expression
description: Take a named function declaration and rewrite it as a function expression assigned to a const, then call it. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the expression form
steps.instructions: Create a const and assign it an unnamed function expression: the `function` keyword with no name after it, followed by the parameter list and body. It should compute and return a value from its parameter.

steps.title: Call it and log the result
steps.instructions: Call your function through the const with a sample argument, and use console.log to print what it returns.

steps.title: Check the shape
steps.instructions: Confirm there is no name between `function` and `(`, and that the whole assignment ends with a semicolon.

requirements.title: Anonymous function assigned to a variable
requirements.description: A const/let/var is assigned a function expression with no name after the function keyword. Help: 3.4.4 (Function Expressions)
requirements.hint: Use const, a name, an equals sign, then the word function with NO name after it, then the parameters and the body.

requirements.title: Function called through the variable
requirements.description: The assigned const is called inside a console.log. Help: 3.4.2 (A Function Is a Value)
requirements.hint: Call the function through the const name you chose, with a sample value, inside console.log.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: The function uses its parameter
requirements.description: The function expression has a parameter and its body uses it. Help: 3.4.4 (Function Expressions)
requirements.hint: Give the function a parameter and compute the returned value from it: function (n) { return n * 2; }.

requirements.title: the call prints a value
requirements.description: At least one line is printed and it is not undefined. Help: 3.4.4 (Function Expressions)
requirements.hint: Call the function through its const and print what it returns. A function with no return prints undefined.

checks.fail: Print the value your function returns: console.log(yourConst(7)). The function needs a return.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.4.5 Lab: Rewrite a Declaration as an Expression". The task they were given: Create a const and assign it an unnamed function expression: the `function` keyword with no name after it, followed by the parameter list and body. It should compute and return a value from its parameter. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
